title: Keyboard shortcuts for an extension with the commands API
when: Users want to trigger a browser extension feature from the keyboard, such as opening its popup or running an action on the current page.
prompt:
Goal: Commands declared in the manifest with sensible default keys, handled in the service worker, and documented with how users change them.
Steps:
1. manifest.json "commands": { "_execute_action": { "suggested_key": { "default": "Ctrl+Shift+Y", "mac": "Command+Shift+Y" }, "description": "Open the popup" }, "toggle-feature": { "suggested_key": { "default": "Alt+Shift+T" }, "description": "Toggle highlighting" } }.
2. At most four commands may suggest keys.
3. Each combo needs Ctrl or Alt (Command or MacCtrl on mac), Shift optional.
4. chrome.commands.onCommand.addListener((command, tab) => ...) at top level; a command grants activeTab, so scripting.executeScript works without host permissions.
5. _execute_action opens the popup and fires no onCommand event.
6. Show real bindings: const all = await chrome.commands.getAll(); an empty shortcut means unassigned, often due to a conflict.
7. Only users can change keys, at chrome://extensions/shortcuts or the browser's shortcut page.
Quality bar:
- Defaults avoid browser shortcuts such as Ctrl+T and Ctrl+W.
- The UI shows the actual key, not the suggested one.
Pitfalls:
- Changing suggested_key in an update and expecting existing users to get it.
- More than four suggested keys, which breaks loading.
Verify:
- [ ] commands block is valid JSON with descriptions.
- [ ] onCommand at top level.
- [ ] getAll used to display bindings.
- [ ] No reserved browser keys.
Output: The commands block in manifest.json, the handler in background.js and a Shortcuts note in README.md.

examples.input: atalho de teclado para ativar minha extensao na pagina atual
examples.output: commands block with _execute_action and toggle-feature, onCommand handler using activeTab, popup showing real keys from commands.getAll
